question: If it takes 5 machines 5 minutes to make 5 widgets, would it take 100 machines 100 minutes to make 100 widgets?

claims.text: 100 machines would make 100 widgets in about 5 minutes, not 100 minutes.
Scaling everything up proportionally might suggest the time also scales up, so it would take 100 minutes.
More widgets means more time, so 100 widgets should take 100 minutes.
Each machine makes one widget in 5 minutes.
With 100 machines each making one widget at the same rate, all finish in 5 minutes.
The extra machines work in parallel, so the number of widgets per machine does not grow.
Time depends on how many widgets each machine must make, not on the total count.
The per-machine rate is what decides the answer.
The answer assumes identical machines, no shared bottleneck, and no setup constraints, which the question implies.
